title: What the Tool Can Push: Force Is the Dual of Speed

questions.question: The Jacobian J gives tool speed from joint speeds. What gives the joint torques for a force at the tool?
options: The transpose of J: power is the same at both ends of a rigid arm, so torque is J transposed times force
questions.explanation: Using J instead of its transpose leaves the first row unchanged and the second wrong, and the elbow torque came out +4.89 where it should be -3.99.

questions.question: Why does the test check the torques against the work done as each joint moves?
options: The principle of virtual work shares no algebra with the Jacobian, so a mistake in one cannot hide in both
questions.explanation: It agreed to 1.9e-09 N m across 1014 poses and forces.

questions.question: Near a straight arm, 0.1 N m of change in a torque changed the implied force by 20.0 N. Why?
options: Going from torques to force inverts a matrix whose determinant is l1 l2 sin(q2), which is nearly zero there, so the inverse is badly conditioned
questions.explanation: A force along a straight arm puts almost no torque on either joint, so the torques say almost nothing about it.

questions.question: Nearly straight, the arm could push 720 N along itself and 20 N across it. Why is the tool so strong along the arm?
options: The load goes down the structure of the arm, so the joints feel almost no torque from it, and the motors' limits are far away
questions.explanation: Exactly straight it is infinite. And along the arm it can hardly move at all, 0.02 m/s, so the direction it cannot move in is the direction it pushes hardest.

questions.question: What does strongest_push do to find the limit?
options: Takes a unit force in the direction, finds the torque each joint needs for it, and scales it until the first joint reaches its limit
questions.explanation: The torque is linear in the force, so it is solved for. Exactly one joint ends on its limit, which the test checks over 24 directions.

questions.question: A datasheet says an arm can push with 20 N. What is missing?
options: The direction and the pose: across the arm it is limited by the motors, along it the structure carries the load, and it changes with the elbow
questions.explanation: The same motors gave 20 N across a nearly straight arm and 720 N along it. A rating without a direction is the best case or the worst.
